thinking: Detailed Phase 1-5 structural scan: Evaluating Trump administration taxpayer-funded political ad campaign. Stated claim: Public service announcements. Reality: Campaign spots funded by taxpayers promoting Donald Trump ahead of midterms. Forces, planes, coordinates computed.
subject: Trump's new ads look like campaign spots. Taxpayers are paying for them.
posts:
When public funds blur into partisan promotion, who really pays the price? Taxpayers bankroll pro-Trump ads disguised as PSAs.
Evidence: Taxpayer funds, campaign ads, White House spin
#Aletheia #USPol

The White House defends taxpayer-funded TV spots featuring Donald Trump as standard public service announcements.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Government funds are airing political spots nearly identical to 2024 campaign ads, glorifying the president ahead of midterms.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.9) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. Taxpayer funds are repurposed for partisan self-promotion under the guise of public service.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 2)

- Trump Administration: FAIL (-0.85, -0.9) — Misuses public funds for political messaging.
- Public Service Label: FAIL (-0.9, -0.85) — Pretext masks partisan branding.
The Trump administration is spending hundreds of thousands of taxpayer dollars to broadcast political spots featuring Donald Trump during major sporting events, prompting bipartisan criticism.

The Bright Side:
Even some Republican lawmakers are publicly pushing back against this blurring of state resources and campaign promotion.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The Plane Error confuses WHAT (partisan campaign spots) with WHO (public servants serving all citizens). The bait-and-switch trades civic duty for personal branding.

Social Physics Analysis:
The administration runs a classic smart selfish maneuver: secret partisan goals wrapped in the pretext of public service announcements, projecting blame onto critics while extracting public funds.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. F_pos outweighs F_neg, driving ψ negative through hidden extraction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public money belongs to the citizenry, not partisan image-building.

The Unavoidable Lie: These political broadcasts are neutral public service announcements.

Alethekanon:
When state machinery becomes a personal campaign vehicle, the boundary between public trust and private extraction dissolves.🌐

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see public resources, built from everyone's hard work, used to divide rather than heal our communities.

Brothekanon:
Using tax dollars to run your own campaign ads while people worry about bills is wild work.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth" Matthew 6:19 FAIL
Using public coffers for personal glory corrupts the sacred trust of leadership.

On Sunday, instead of ads for pizza deals from Papa John's or the latest insurance pitch from Jake at State Farm, fans watching their favorite NFL or college football teams were shown a 30-second, black-and-white video of President Donald Trump. The ad, nearly identical to an ad released by the Trump presidential campaign in 2024, shows the president silently walking down a hallway, while his voiceover warns of a "final battle" to "cast out the communists, Marxists, and fascists" and "liberate America from these villains once and for all."

There was one noticeable difference. The ad that aired Sunday was "Paid for by the U.S. Government," courtesy of American taxpayers. Stated Claim / Post Context:
Mamdani refuses request to send Trump a selfie of him and Kimmel

Zohran Mamdani has refused to send President Donald Trump the selfie of himself with Jimmy Kimmel.  During an episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live on Monday (28 September), Mamdani appeared as a guest on the show where Kimmel asked whether the New York mayor could send Trump the selfie of two of them from the studio.   Mamdani drew laughter from the audience with his response: “Jimmy, I love you, but I love housing more”.  Kimmel also asked Mamdani about the US president’s texting style , whether he texts in all caps like the way he posts. Mamdani gave a brief and polite answer. “ Pretty standard”.
